notes: Fictional object insert (ABox): a made-up new value (a newly described living species) of a real, well-known subject (the tuatara genus Sphenodon) in a relation that holds several values (a genus has species). Rewritten from the earlier subject insert on the same made-up name: the real genus is now the subject, so a method that edits at the subject starts from everything it holds about the tuatara. It could exist unrecorded: the Brothers Island tuatara was described as a second species (S. guntheri, recognised 1989) and treated as a subspecies since 2009, so a newly split island lineage is the kind of thing taxonomists report. The direct question singles out the new value. Determinate: the chain through the genus to the reptiles and "not a lizard". Indeterminate (background beliefs): the famous uniqueness of the tuatara and its count. R1: the closed fact is current consensus. Near query: the tuatara stays in New Zealand.
